## Overview

This script consolidates processed data from four distinct survey streams: Apprenticeship (APPSO), Trades (TRD), Baccalaureate (BGS), and Diploma/Associate/Certificate (DACSO).  The datasets are merged into a single, unified "Master Cohort" table.

It requires the successful completion of all prior ingestion scripts; the presence of Outcomes datasets and lookup tables are checked for existence before execution.

## Methodology Overview

### Cross-Survey Compatibility

The routine executes four major functions to ensure cross-survey compatibility:

1. Model-Year Weighting:
The script filters the central weight table for the 2022-2023 model year and joins it to each survey stream. This ensures that every respondent's contribution is scaled appropriately for provincial labor market representation.

2. Labour Supply Derivation:
While each survey asks about employment differently, this script translates those unique responses into a standardized NEW_LABOUR_SUPPLY variable.

TRD/APPSO: Based on LABR_EMPLOYED and LABR_IN_LABOUR_MARKET status.

BGS/DACSO: Uses complex CASE logic involving CURRENT_ACTIVITY (e.g., working vs. seeking vs. further study).

3. Composite Analytical Key Construction:
The script generates composite keys LCIP4_CRED and LCIP2_CRED. These keys concatenate graduation status, CIP codes, training markers, and credential types into a single string to allow for precise matching against labor market demand.

4. Cohort Aggregation and Refresh:
The script manages a "Master Cohort" table (t_cohorts_recoded). It appends new records for TRD and APPSO while performing a "delete-and-replace" refresh for BGS and DACSO to ensure the longitudinal dataset remains current without duplication.

#### Data Dictionary

##### t_cohorts_recoded

<ul class="list-variable-names">
  <li>PEN (Number): The Personal Education Number, a unique identifier for students in the BC education system.</li>
  <li>STQU_ID (String): A unique survey identifier prepended with the survey type (e.g., "BGS - 12345").</li>
  <li>SURVEY (String): A character code representing the specific survey source (e.g., "BGS", "DACSO", "TRD", "APPSO").</li>
  <li>SURVEY_YEAR (Number): The calendar year in which the survey data was collected.</li>
  <li>INST_CD (String): A character code representing the post-secondary institution.</li>
  <li>LCIP_CD (String): The 2-digit Classification of Instructional Programs (CIP) family identifier.</li>
  <li>LCP4_CD (String): The 4-digit CIP code identifier for the specific program.</li>
  <li>TTRAIN (Number): A numeric marker indicating if technical training was part of the program.</li>
  <li>NOC_CD (String): The 5-digit National Occupational Classification code representing the graduate's employment.</li>
  <li>AGE_AT_SURVEY (Number): The age of the respondent at the time of the survey.</li>
  <li>AGE_GROUP (Number): A numeric binning code representing the student's age cohort.</li>
  <li>AGE_GROUP_ROLLUP (Number): A higher-level numeric code used to aggregate age groups for broader analysis.</li>
  <li>GRAD_STATUS (String): A code indicating whether the student graduated or completed their program.</li>
  <li>RESPONDENT (Number): A binary flag indicating if the student successfully completed the survey.</li>
  <li>NEW_LABOUR_SUPPLY (Number): A derived indicator representing the student's entry or status in the labor market.</li>
  <li>WEIGHT (Number): The statistical weight applied to the record to ensure provincial representativeness.</li>
  <li>PSSM_CREDENTIAL (String): The standardized credential name (e.g., "BACH" for Bachelor's degree).</li>
  <li>PSSM_CRED (String): A composite field combining graduation status and credential type.</li>
  <li>LCIP4_CRED (String): A high-resolution composite key combining CIP code, training markers, and credential.</li>
  <li>LCIP2_CRED (String): A mid-resolution composite key using the 2-digit CIP family and credential.</li>
  <li>CURRENT_REGION_PSSM_CODE (Number): The standardized regional code where the respondent currently resides.</li>
  <li>AGE_AT_GRAD (Number): A placeholder for the student's age at the time of graduation.</li>
  <li>AGE_GRAD_GROUP (Number): A placeholder for the age cohort grouping at the time of graduation.</li>
  <li>AGE_GRAD_GROUP_ROLLUP (Number): A placeholder for the aggregated age grouping at graduation.</li>
  <li>OLD_LABOUR_SUPPLY (Number): A legacy indicator for labor force entry used for comparison.</li>
  <li>WEIGHT_NLS (Number): A placeholder for specific weighting related to New Labour Supply.</li>
  <li>WEIGHT_OCC (Number): A placeholder for specific weighting related to occupational outcomes.</li>
  <li>WEIGHT_AGE (Number): A placeholder for specific weighting related to age distribution.</li>
  <li>NEW_LABOUR_SUPPLY_CIP_NOC (Number): A placeholder for labor supply indicators specifically mapped to CIP and NOC combinations.</li>
  <li>WEIGHT_NLS_CIP_NOC (Number): A placeholder for specific weights used in CIP-NOC labor supply analysis.</li>
  <li>WEIGHT_OCC_CIP_NOC (Number): A placeholder for weights used in CIP-NOC occupational analysis.</li>
  <li>ENDDT (Date): A placeholder for the record end date or survey completion date.</li>
</ul>

##### t_dacso_data_part_1

<ul class="list-variable-names">

  <li>COCI_INST_CD (String): The administrative code for the post-secondary institution.</li>

  <li>LCIP_CD (String): The 2-digit CIP code family identifier.</li>

  <li>COCI_AGE_AT_SURVEY (Number): The respondent's age at the time they completed the survey.</li>
  <li>COSC_GRAD_STATUS_LGDS_CD_GROUP (Number): A numeric group code classifying the student's graduation or completion status.</li>
  <li>RESPONDENT (Number): A flag indicating if the student successfully responded to the survey.</li>
  <li>NEW_LABOUR_SUPPLY (Number): A derived indicator representing the student's status as a new entry into the labor force.</li>
  <li>OLD_LABOUR_SUPPLY (Number): A legacy indicator for labor force entry (used for longitudinal comparison).</li>
  <li>HAD_PREVIOUS_CREDENTIAL (Number): A binary flag indicating if the student held a post-secondary credential prior to this program.</li>
  <li>PFST_IN_POST_SEC_BEFORE (Number): A binary flag indicating if the student had enrolled in post-secondary education previously.</li>
  <li>PRGM_CREDENTIAL_AWARDED (String): The raw administrative code for the credential awarded to the student.</li>
  <li>CURRENT_REGION_PSSM_CODE (Number): The standardized PSSM regional code for the respondent's current residence.</li>
  <li>PRGM_CREDENTIAL_AWARDED_NAME (String): The descriptive name of the specific credential awarded.</li>
  <li>PSSM_CREDENTIAL (String): The standardized credential code used for Provincial Student Survey Modeling.</li>
  <li>PSSM_CREDENTIAL_NAME (String): The full descriptive name of the PSSM-standardized credential.</li>
  <li>AGE_GROUP (Number): The numeric bin identifier for the student's age cohort.</li>
  <li>AGE_GROUP_ROLLUP (Number): A higher-level numeric code used for aggregated age reporting.</li>
  <li>LCIP4_CRED (String): A composite analytical key combining graduation status, CIP-4 code, training, and credential.</li>
  <li>PFST_HAD_PREVIOUS_CDTL (Number): A raw indicator from the outcomes file regarding previous credentials held.</li>
  <li>PFST_FURSTDY_INCL_STILL_ATTD (Number): An indicator of whether the respondent is engaged in further study or still attending.</li>
  <li>WEIGHT (Number): The statistical weight assigned to the record for model-year analysis.</li>

## Suggested Improvements

- The script resets `t_cohorts_recoded` by filtering it to zero rows before rebuilding it. Initializing a new object explicitly would make the refresh behaviour clearer and less dependent on pre-existing state.
- Model-year strings such as `2022-2023` and `2023/2024` are embedded in several joins and survey labels. Moving those values into a shared configuration object would simplify annual rollover.
- PTIB inclusion is controlled by `ptib_run`, but the same PTIB responsibility is referenced again in later modules. A single documented handoff point would make the private-institution path easier to maintain.
- The script contains survey-specific transformation blocks with similar age, weight, and credential recoding steps. Extracting survey adapters would reduce the size of the main build routine.
- Required input names are aliased at the top (`appso_data_final`, `bgs_data_final`, `bgs_inst_recode`) because the loader outputs do not match the processing names. Harmonizing those names upstream would reduce confusion.

## Additional Details

This script is the integration point between the cohort loaders and the labour-supply calculations. It explicitly consumes `trd_data`, `trd_graduates`, `t_appso_data_final`, `appso_graduates`, `t_bgs_data_final`, `t_bgs_inst_recode`, `t_bgs_data_final_for_outcomesmatching`, `t_weights`, `t_dacso_data_part_1_stepa`, age and region lookup tables, `t_year_survey_year`, `qry_private_credentials_06d1_cohort_dist`, and `T_DACSO_Near_Completers_RatiosAgeAtGradCIP4_TTRAIN_r`. It writes the unified cohort table `t_cohorts_recoded_r` and an updated `t_dacso_data_part_1_r`. Those outputs feed directly into the labour-supply and occupation-distribution scripts in Module 02b and are also expected by Module 07 through `load-program-projections.R`. The script uses `regular_run`, `qi_run`, and `ptib_run` flags to control weighting and PTIB inclusion.
